note: The refusal path crashes while refusing. Hex has no conversion limit in CPython, so lex() builds the integer happily and the typer correctly decides it does not fit in int64. Then typer.py writes the diagnosis -- f'integer literal {e.value} does not fit in int64' -- and interpolating a 20,000-bit integer into an f-string IS a decimal conversion, which is the thing CPython caps at 4300 digits. The ValueError is raised from inside the raise. The verdict was right and the sentence explaining it is what fell over, on the branch that only ever runs on input someone else wrote.
signature: ValueError in typer._check_expr: Exceeds the limit (N digits) for integer string conversion;
